title: Augmented derived tower unit with all-object ordinary normalization
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_0,\mathcal C_1,\mathcal D_0,\mathcal D_1$ be categories, $q:\mathcal C_0	o\mathcal D_0$ a localization at a class $W$ of arrows [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], and $q':\mathcal C_1	o\mathcal D_1$ a functor. Let $G,T:\mathcal C_0	o\mathcal C_1$, $F:\mathcal C_1	o\mathcal C_0$, $DG,LT:\mathcal D_0	o\mathcal D_1$ and $RF:\mathcal D_1	o\mathcal D_0$ be functors. Give natural transformations $
u:1_{\mathcal C_0}	o FG$, $\eta:G	o T$, $\gamma:qF	o RFq'$, an isomorphism $\alpha:DGq\cong q'G$, and $ eta:LTq	o q'T$. Assume $(LT, eta)$ is a universal right Kan extension of $q'T$ along $q$, meaning that every $a:Hq	o q'T$ factors uniquely as $ eta(bq)$ with $b:H	o LT$.
There is a unique natural $t:DG	o LT$ with $ eta_Xt_{qX}=q'(\eta_X)\alpha_X$. There is a unique natural $v:1_{\mathcal D_0}	o RF\,DG$ with $RF(\alpha_X)v_{qX}=\gamma_{GX}q(
u_X)$, for all $X\in\mathcal C_0$. For the natural map $c=RF(t)\circ v:1_{\mathcal D_0}	o RF\,LT$, one has
$$RF( eta_X)c_{qX}=\gamma_{TX}\,q igl(F(\eta_X)
u_X igr)\qquad(X\in\mathcal C_0).$$
Composition is right to left. When $G=\Delta$ is the constant strict tower functor, $F=\lim$, $
u$ its ordinary adjunction unit, and $T$ an augmented tower functor with augmentation $\eta$ [def-weil-inverse-system], this formula normalizes the completion map by the actual ordinary cochain map $X	o\lim T(X)$. With a chosen functor $RF=R\lim$ and ordinary-to-derived comparison $\gamma$, the equation holds on every complex, without requiring it to be a resolving representative. Here the functor and comparison are supplied data; the derived-limit property [def-weil-derived-limit] by itself does not choose either of them. The assertion does not require invertibility of $ eta_X$ or $\gamma_Y$, or an adjunction between the cochain functors.

proof.text: Put $a_X=q'(\eta_X)\alpha_X:DG(qX)\to q'(TX)$. It is natural, being the composite of $\alpha$ with $q'$ applied to $\eta$. Apply the right Kan universal property assumed in the statement with $H=DG$ and $a$. It gives a unique $t:DG\to LT$ with $\beta_Xt_{qX}=a_X$. This is exactly the asserted characterization of $t$. In Lean use Functor.liftOfIsRightKanExtension, its fac_app lemma, and hom_ext_of_isRightKanExtension.

proof.text: Define $d_X=RF(\alpha_X^{-1})\gamma_{GX}q(\nu_X):qX\to RF(DG(qX))$. These components are natural: they compose $q\nu$, $\gamma$ whiskered by $G$, and $RF$ applied to the inverse natural isomorphism $\alpha$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with $L=q$, target category $\mathcal D_0$, $F_1=q$, $F_2=(RF\,DG)q$, lifts $F'_1=1_{\mathcal D_0}$ and $F'_2=RF\,DG$, identity comparison isomorphisms, and $\tau=d$. Both source functors invert $W$, since $q$ does and functors preserve isomorphisms. The cited clause gives a unique natural $v$ with $v_{qX}=d_X$. Multiplying by $RF(\alpha_X)$ gives the required equation for $v$. Conversely that equation implies $v_{qX}=d_X$ by cancellation of the specified isomorphism, so the same uniqueness applies. In Lean assemble d by whiskering with the functor associators and unitors, then use Localization.liftNatTrans and Localization.natTrans_ext.

proof.text:
Define $c=RF(t)\circ v$; whiskering and composition of natural transformations make it natural. Functoriality of $RF$, the equation defining $t$, the equation defining $v$, and naturality of $\gamma$ at $\eta_X:GX\to TX$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
RF(\beta_X)c_{qX}
&=RF(\beta_Xt_{qX})v_{qX}\\
&=RF(q'(\eta_X))RF(\alpha_X)v_{qX}\\
&=RF(q'(\eta_X))\gamma_{GX}q(\nu_X)\\
&=\gamma_{TX}q(F(\eta_X))q(\nu_X)\\
&=\gamma_{TX}q(F(\eta_X)\nu_X).
\end{aligned}$$
Every equality is at the given object $X$; only $\alpha$ was inverted, so neither $\beta_X$ nor $\gamma_{TX}$ need be invertible.

proof.text:
For the tower specialization, write $p_n:\lim T(X)	o T(X)_n$ for the limit projections, and $r_n:\lim\Delta X	o X$ for those of the constant tower. The ordinary adjunction unit has $r_n
u_X=1_X$. By the definition of the morphism of towers $\eta_X$ [def-weil-inverse-system], the map induced on limits satisfies $p_nF(\eta_X)=(\eta_X)_nr_n$. Thus $p_nF(\eta_X)
u_X=(\eta_X)_n$ for every $n$. The limit universal property identifies $F(\eta_X)
u_X$ with the actual ordinary map induced by the augmentation cone. Substitution in Step 3 proves the claimed ordinary-map normalization on every complex. In this specialization $RF$ and $\gamma$ remain supplied data; no functor or comparison is extracted from the Roos-triangle property of [def-weil-derived-limit]. The contextual derived-limit definition is not used by this proof; Limits.limit.hom_ext, limMap_π and the definition of constLimAdj suffice.
